title: Re-derive CVG-052, CVG-053, CVG-057 and CVG-066 — wave 4 moved them toward spec and their probes went red
description:
Serves documents.v1 (CVG-052/053), surface.v1 (CVG-057/066). Found while working converge-jc9, which owned only the six rows named in that item and deliberately did not guess at these four.

`uv run --with pyyaml ledger/checks/verify.py` at 10a8d76 (after converge-jc9's edits) reports 4 of 35 executable refs not meeting their expect. Every one of them is drift TOWARD spec — LEDGER-FORMAT §3 says that is drift too, and must be re-derived rather than quietly enjoyed:

  CVG-052  expected  DOCUMENTS-RULE-IDS contract_clauses_bold_led,contrac…
           got       DOCUMENTS-RULE-IDS changelog_entries_carry_evidence,clause_numbers_match_the_rule_table,contract_clauses_bold_led,…
  CVG-053  same pinned rule-id list, same break
  CVG-057  expected  STATE-WORDS-ASSERTED=1-OF-8   got  STATE-WORDS-ASSERTED=2-OF-8
  CVG-066  expected  NO-VOCABULARY-SCAN-AGAINST-THE-APP   got  VOCABULARY-SCAN-WIRED

CVG-052/CVG-053 were forecast by the ledger's own header: wave 4 renumbers the documents kit's rules to documents.v1's Core clauses 1..13, "which would break CVG-052/CVG-053's pinned rule-id list by design". The forecast was right. CVG-057 and CVG-066 are the surface side of the same wave.

Two further things a holder should fix in the same pass, both left alone by converge-jc9 for the same ownership reason:

1. STALE RULE NUMBERS THROUGHOUT THE documents.v1 SECTION. The renumber means `indexed` refs like "conformance/documents/run.py (rule 1c)" (CVG-041), "(rule 1d)" (CVG-047), "(rule 2a)" (CVG-048), "(rule 2b)" (CVG-062), "(rules 5a, 5b)" (CVG-054) and "(rule 6)" (CVG-055) now name rules that either do not exist or belong to a DIFFERENT clause. verify.py cannot catch this: an `indexed` ref is only checked for path existence, and the path still exists. converge-jc9 corrected only the two `proves` lines that named rows it was moving (CVG-047, CVG-062) and left the rest.

2. THE `indexed` REFS ARE THE WEAK FORM. converge-jc9 gave all seven of its rows executable probes with a distinctive token for both outcomes, negative-controlled in a scratch copy. The CONFORMS rows around them still cite a file path that cannot fail. Promoting them is the cheap half of this item.
</description>
<parameter name="acceptance">GIVEN the documents and surface kits as merged at 10a8d76 WHEN CVG-052, CVG-053, CVG-057 and CVG-066 are each re-derived against the rule that now answers them THEN `uv run --with pyyaml ledger/checks/verify.py` prints "[OK  ] N executable refs, each meeting its declared expect" and exits 0, with that output shown; AND every `indexed` ref in the documents.v1 section names a rule number that appears in `uv run conformance/documents/run.py . --json-only`, shown by printing both lists; AND no row is moved on the strength of this item's summary alone.

title: conformance/README.md says every kit numbers to the Conformance-asserts bullets; the documents kit no longer does
description:
Found while closing converge-bmp.

conformance/README.md, section "Numbering follows the contract", says:

  "Every rule row is numbered to its contract's **Conformance kit asserts** bullet."

That is now true of the composition and surface kits only. The documents kit is numbered to documents.v1's Core clause numbers (1..13), because the bullet numbering hid a real gap: the bullet list carries seven bullets for thirteen clauses, so Core 10 and Core 11 had no bullet, therefore no row, therefore nothing visibly missing.

The shared README is outside conformance/documents/**, so the lane that made the change could not update it.

Two things to settle, in order:
1. The steward's ruling on contracts/documents.v2-candidate.md change 2 (which numbering clause 5 means). Filed as converge-bmp's residual.
2. Whichever way it goes, conformance/README.md's numbering paragraph needs one edit — and if the Core-clause reading is ratified, the composition and surface kit rule tables renumber to their contracts' Core clauses, and documents kit rule 5b can stop reporting a divergence.

Reproduce:
  uv run conformance/documents/run.py . --json-only | python3 -c "import json,sys;print([x for x in json.load(sys.stdin)['results'] if x['rule']=='5b'][0]['observed'])"

---

CLOSED WITH AN UNMET ACCEPTANCE CLAUSE — read this before trusting the status.

This item was resolved on 2026-09-03 by lane w4-doc-kit-2, and its status reads "resolved". Only the first half of its acceptance was actually met. The status alone is misleading, so the fact is recorded on the item rather than only inside the resolution text.

Met: "conformance/README.md ... its numbering paragraph describes what the three kits actually do" — commit acc77b8 replaced the false sentence with the measured per-kit anchor table.

NOT met: "AND documents kit rule 5b reports every contract aligned with its kit's rule table." Its own GIVEN ("a ruling on documents.v2-candidate change 2") never occurred. Rule 5b still reports 1 of 3 aligned, with composition.v1 and surface.v1 listed as not aligned, and that is correct behaviour — 5b refuses to fail another kit on a reading the steward has not ratified.

Note also that this item's description above and its acceptance sentence disagreed with each other: the description framed the work as "one edit, whichever way it goes", while the acceptance additionally required an aligned 5b that only a ratification can produce. That contradiction is what let the item look closeable. It is named here so the next reader does not have to rediscover it.

The unmet half now lives in converge-duf (linked follow-up-of this item), which is blocked on the steward's word rather than sitting in the ready queue.
acceptance: GIVEN a ruling on documents.v2-candidate change 2 WHEN conformance/README.md is read THEN its numbering paragraph describes what the three kits actually do; AND documents kit rule 5b reports every contract aligned with its kit's rule table.

title: modes surface by bundle-root auto-discovery, not by a `modes:` include block — and a stale app-bundle namespace hides them
description:
Measured while wiring converge-axv (2026-09-02, this machine).

FINDING 1 — the `modes:` include block is not the mechanism. hooks-mode's ModeDiscovery._ensure_bundle_discovery (amplifier-bundle-modes, modules/hooks-mode/amplifier_module_hooks_mode/__init__.py:303-372) walks EVERY composed bundle namespace from the mention_resolver and adds `<bundle base_path>/modes` as a search path if that directory exists. amplifier_foundation never parses a top-level `modes:` key at all (grep: only validate_modes(), a schema-only scan of `modes/*.md`). Controlled A/B on the --app path, same environment, block present vs. block removed: `converge-manager` listed in BOTH runs. So the block is a declaration of intent (and matches amplifier-online's convention) but carries no load today.

FINDING 2 — the real cause of "a session that adds the behavior never sees the mode" on this machine is NAMESPACE SHADOWING. Two stale GitHub converge app bundles (bkrabach/… and microsoft/amplifier-bundle-converge@main#subdirectory=behaviors/converge.yaml) register the `converge` namespace, and their cached checkouts (~/.amplifier/cache/amplifier-bundle-converge-*) contain NO modes/ directory. With them registered, `@converge:modes/converge-manager.md` resolves to nothing and the mode never lists — even with the block present and the local behavior added --app. Removing just those two app entries made `converge-manager` appear immediately.

Consequence worth deciding: the mode reaches a --app user only once a checkout carrying modes/ is what the `converge` namespace resolves to (i.e. after publish + cache refresh), and a user with an older converge app bundle registered will keep shadowing it. Two candidate follow-ups: (a) document the auto-discovery mechanism where composition is described, so the next session does not assume the block is load-bearing; (b) decide whether anything should detect/flag a duplicate `converge` namespace registration rather than silently first-wins.
acceptance: GIVEN a reader of the converge composition docs WHEN they ask "what makes a mode visible to a composed session" THEN they find the auto-discovery mechanism named (bundle-root modes/ dir per composed namespace), not just the `modes:` include convention; AND the duplicate-namespace shadowing failure mode is written down somewhere a user hitting it can find it.

title: The app never says whether a contract is Kept — Direction shows Draft/Locked only (surface.v1 Core 8, kit rule 8b)
description:
Measured with the retargeted surface kit against the running app (uv run conformance/surface/run.py http://127.0.0.1:8097 --changes-nothing '/direction/*/mark-read'):

  [FAIL] 8b  no contract is shown as Kept · Not yet · Broken · Pinned open · Can't check — the state beside each one is ['Draft'], which is the document's own status, not whether the promise is being kept

surface.v1 Core 8 fixes two vocabularies. The lane one is spoken: lane cards on Operation say Working / Quiet / Silent — may have died (kit rule 8a passes, 111 states shown, every one a plain word). The contract one is never spoken anywhere. src/amplifier_converge/words.py defines CONTRACT_STATES and maps the internal tokens onto them (conforms -> Kept, gap -> Not yet, violation -> Broken, open pinned -> Pinned open, ...), but nothing reads the ledger: `grep -rn "ledger\|rows.yaml\|CONFORMS" src` returns only words.py itself and the lane/queue/document readers, none of which touch ledger/rows.yaml.

So Direction shows five contracts each chipped `Draft` — the document's own status from its H1, which is documents.v1 clause 6, not surface.v1 clause 8. A steward opening Direction cannot see whether a promise is being kept, which is the whole of clause 8's first half.

ledger/rows.yaml is seeded (62 rows, each carrying a disposition), so the reading exists on disk; what is missing is a reader and a chip.

Owning path: src/amplifier_converge/reading/ (a ledger reader mapping each contract to its rows' worst disposition through words.surface_word) and src/amplifier_converge/web/pages.py (_document_row, to show it beside the Draft/Locked chip rather than instead of it).

Not fixed here: lane w5-surface-kit owns conformance/surface/** only; src/ is explicitly out of scope. The kit rule that catches this is new and stays FAIL until the app speaks the words.
acceptance: GIVEN the companion app reading a project whose ledger is seeded WHEN Direction is opened THEN each contract shows one of Kept · Not yet · Broken · Pinned open · Can't check against reality, alongside its own Draft/Locked status; AND `uv run conformance/surface/run.py <the running app>` reports rule 8b PASS.

title: Documents: Core 5 says clause numbers match the kit's rule table, but kits number to the Conformance-asserts bullets
description:
Found while seeding ledger/rows.yaml (converge-5m8); recorded as ledger row CVG-046, disposition OPEN-PINNED.

documents.v1 Core 5 ends: "Numbers match the conformance kit's rule table."

The three shipped kits number their rules to the contract's **Conformance kit asserts** bullets, not to its Core clause numbers. conformance/composition/README.md says so in its own words: "Rows are numbered to the contract's **Conformance kit asserts** bullets." So composition kit rule "1a" is conformance bullet 1, not Core clause 1 — and Core clause 1 has no rule numbered 1.

Two readings, both defensible, and the clause does not settle it:
(a) the kit's rules should be numbered to the Core clauses (the teeth), so a failing rule names the clause it breaks; or
(b) numbering to the conformance bullets is correct, and the clause means the bullets.

This is an interpretive call about what documents.v1 requires, not a defect in the kits. One sentence from the intent steward settles it; whichever way it goes, either the clause or the three kit rule tables get one edit.

Not a blocker: no kit or ledger row depends on the answer today.
acceptance: GIVEN documents.v1 Core 5's last sentence WHEN the steward has ruled THEN either the clause names which numbering it means, or the three kit rule tables renumber to the Core clauses; AND ledger row CVG-046 moves off OPEN-PINNED.

title: Upstream ask: `amplifier tool invoke` never emits tool:pre, so no hook can guard it
description:
Upstream ask arising from converge-ldz. Converge has closed this at the bundle layer, but the hole is generic and belongs upstream.

WHAT: `amplifier_app_cli/commands/tool.py::_invoke_tool_from_bundle_async` builds a full session (hooks mount correctly; measured: candidate-guard IS registered on tool:pre) and then calls `tool_instance.execute(tool_args)` DIRECTLY. No `tool:pre` is emitted, so no hook registered on that event can see, veto, or even observe the call. `tool:post` and `tool:error` are likewise never emitted on this path.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND CONVERGE: every bundle that guards, audits, redacts, or logs via `tool:pre`/`tool:post` silently loses coverage on this path. In the session measured, nine handlers were registered on tool:pre (mode-tools, approval_hook, streaming-ui-tool-pre, session-event-persister, hooks-todo-display-pre, candidate-guard, hook-redaction, hooks-logging, LoggingHandler). None of them ran. That includes the approval hook, so a tool the user configured to require approval executes without one via this path.

EVIDENCE: in a scratch repo holding a contract locked per contracts/documents.v1 clause 6, `amplifier tool invoke write_file file_path=contracts/probe.v1.md content=hijacked -b <bundle>` reported success and wrote the file (128 bytes -> 8), while the same module's own evaluate_tool_pre() denies that byte-identical input.

CONVERGE'S WORKAROUND (not the fix): hooks-candidate-guard now also wraps each mounted tool instance's own execute() at mount time, which works because amplifier_core/_session_init.py mounts tools BEFORE hooks. Every bundle needing this protection would have to re-implement the same wrap, which is why it belongs upstream.

SUGGESTED FIX: route `tool invoke` through the same tool-execution path the orchestrator uses, so the standard tool:pre / tool:post / tool:error lifecycle fires; or, if direct dispatch is deliberate, document it as an unhooked path so bundle authors do not assume hook coverage they do not have.

RELATED, SAME FILE FAMILY: composing a session for a bundle under test silently loads a DIFFERENT copy of a module when an app bundle from another source registers the same module name (app bundles compose onto every session and composition dedupes to one). Workaround found: a project-local `.amplifier/settings.local.yaml` containing `bundle: {app: []}` scopes the exclusion to one directory with no global mutation. Worth documenting for anyone testing a local module.
acceptance: GIVEN a bundle that registers a hook on tool:pre AND a repo holding a file that hook would deny writes to WHEN `amplifier tool invoke write_file file_path=<that file> content=...` runs with that bundle composed THEN the hook fires and the write is denied — OR the non-coverage is documented as intended behavior in the app-CLI docs, so bundle authors do not assume hook coverage on this path that they do not have.

title: Numbering anchor: renumber the composition and surface kit rule tables once the steward rules on documents.v2-candidate change 2
description:
Serves documents.v1 clause 5 ("Numbers match the conformance kit's rule table").

This is the half of converge-19b's acceptance that was NOT met when converge-19b was closed. It is recorded here as an open item rather than left as prose inside a resolution, because a reader scanning statuses cannot see an unmet clause buried in a closing note.

converge-19b's stored acceptance read, in full:

  "GIVEN a ruling on documents.v2-candidate change 2 WHEN conformance/README.md is read THEN its numbering paragraph describes what the three kits actually do; AND documents kit rule 5b reports every contract aligned with its kit's rule table."

The first half shipped (commit acc77b8: the numbering section now carries the measured per-kit table). The second half did not, and could not: its own GIVEN never occurred. Clause 5 still does not say which numbering it means, contracts/documents.v2-candidate.md is unanswered, and rule 5b deliberately refuses to fail another kit on an unratified reading -- so it still reports "1 of 3 contract(s) are numbered to their kit's rule table; not aligned: [contracts/composition.v1.md, contracts/surface.v1.md]".

This is the third close in a chain that handed the same residue forward: converge-bmp closed with its acceptance unmet and named converge-19b; converge-19b closed with its acceptance unmet and named only a resolution string. Stopping that here.

Two things must happen, in order, and only the first is a person's:

1. The intent steward answers contracts/documents.v2-candidate.md change 2 with one word. That is owner attention budget item 1 (ratify a contract change) and belongs to nobody else. Not tracked as engineering work.

2. If the Core-clause reading is ratified: renumber conformance/composition/README.md's rule table (ids 1-4, currently anchored to its four Conformance-asserts bullets) and conformance/surface/README.md's (ids 1-5, currently anchored to its five bullets) to their contracts' Core clause numbers -- composition.v1 has seven Core clauses, surface.v1 has ten -- and give each kit's self-test the equivalent of the documents kit's test_every_core_clause_has_a_row. Under a bullet anchor no kit can tell you whether a Core clause went unchecked, because there is no row to be missing; grep confirms neither test file mentions core_clause today. If instead the bullet reading is ratified, the documents kit renumbers back and rule 5b's comparison inverts.

Either way, rule 5b then stops reporting a divergence and conformance/README.md's numbering section collapses to one anchor -- it already says so.

Reproduce the current state:
  uv run conformance/documents/run.py . --json-only | python3 -c "import json,sys;print(*[x for x in json.load(sys.stdin)['results'] if x['rule']=='5b'][0]['observed'],sep=chr(10))"
acceptance: GIVEN the steward has answered contracts/documents.v2-candidate.md change 2 WHEN conformance/documents/run.py runs against this repository THEN rule 5b reports every contract numbered to its kit's rule table, with no contract listed as not aligned; AND each of the three kits' self-tests contains a check that every Core clause of its contract has a rule row, so a clause added later cannot go unchecked without a test failing; AND conformance/README.md's numbering section names one anchor rather than two.

title: lane-brief genre: an evidence-printing criterion must state the falsity condition, not only the presence condition
description:
Serves documents.v1. Ruled a brief defect (not a lane defect) by converge:protocol-authority, 2026-09-03, on review of lane w4-doc-kit-2's close.

WHAT THE BRIEF SAID

Lane w4-doc-kit-2's acceptance criterion 4 read, verbatim:

  "4. Both items resolved; each stored reason printed via work_list read-back."

WHAT HAPPENED

Both items were resolved and both reasons were printed — so the criterion was met exactly as written. But one of the two stored reasons contained a false paragraph, and the tracker will not let a resolution be corrected once an item closes (filed as work_tracker item work_item_pipeline-03c). The lane superseded the record and disclosed the defect, and the criterion still read PASS.

That produced a genuine, repeated disagreement about whether the lane had met its goal: the criterion's literal text was satisfied while its evident purpose — trustworthy evidence — was not. Under PROTOCOL.md section 7 the literal reading governs, because re-reading a briefed criterion at grading time to mean something stricter is a self-ratified amendment of the brief, which is forbidden to lanes and to the orchestrator alike. So the lane closed as SUCCESS-with-residual, correctly, and the ambiguity survived.

THE DEFECT

PROTOCOL.md section 4 requires a lane brief to carry an honesty gate: name what "not proven" looks like before work starts. Criterion 4 named what ABSENT evidence looks like — a reason not printed — and never named what FALSE evidence looks like. That omission is why the two readings could diverge at all.

THE CHANGE

The lane-brief genre should require that any criterion whose evidence is an artifact the lane itself authors states both conditions:

  - the presence condition: the artifact exists and is shown
  - the falsity condition: what makes the shown artifact unsound, and what the lane must do if it discovers its own artifact is wrong after it is written

Criterion 4 would then have read something closer to: "Both items resolved; each stored reason printed via work_list read-back; if a printed reason is found to be false, the correction must be reachable from the reason itself, not only from a linked item."

Applies to future briefs. It does not regrade w4-doc-kit-2, which finished against the version it was briefed on (PROTOCOL.md section 5).

The skill to change is skills/lane-brief.
acceptance: GIVEN the lane-brief skill WHEN an author writes a criterion whose evidence is an artifact the lane itself produces THEN the skill requires them to state what makes that artifact unsound, alongside what makes it present; AND it says what a lane must do when it finds its own evidence wrong after writing it; AND a worked example shows a criterion written both ways, so an author can see which one survives a lane that made a mistake and caught it.

title: Documents: contract clause 4 is silent on whether a contract may carry an EXTRA section
description:
Surfaced while building the documents.v1 conformance kit — an interpretive gap the kit refused to decide on the steward's behalf.

documents.v1 Core 4 says: "The same sections, in the same order, every time. Purpose -> Core (the teeth) -> What v1 deliberately does NOT freeze (with promotion triggers) -> Conformance kit asserts -> Reserved / open questions -> Changelog only if amended."

It fixes PRESENCE and ORDER. It does not say whether a SEVENTH section is permitted.

contracts/operation.v1.md carries one: "## Declared dependencies (checked at install)", between Core and "What v1 deliberately does NOT freeze".

Two readings, both defensible:
  (a) "the same sections ... every time" fixes the SET — an extra section is a violation, and operation.v1 should fold that content into an existing section.
  (b) The clause fixes order and required presence only — an extra section is fine, and the kit should stay quiet.

The kit implements neither ruling. Rule 1b asserts only what the contract unambiguously fixes (presence and order) and REPORTS any extra section in the row's detail, so the fact is visible without inventing a rule:

  contracts/operation.v1.md -> all five required sections, in order
    (also carries: ['Declared dependencies (checked at install)'])

Deciding this is a documents.v1 amendment (a clarifying sentence in clause 4), not a code change. If reading (a) wins, rule 1b tightens to fail an extra section and operation.v1 needs an edit; if (b) wins, clause 4 should say so explicitly so the next reader does not re-derive this question.

Reproduce:
  uv run conformance/documents/run.py . --json-only | python3 -c "import json,sys;[print(f['file'],'->',f['detail']) for x in json.load(sys.stdin)['results'] if x['rule']=='1b' for f in x['files']]"
acceptance: GIVEN documents.v1 clause 4 WHEN a reader asks "may a contract carry a section beyond the six listed?" THEN the clause answers it in one sentence — and if the answer is no, conformance/documents rule 1b fails an extra section and contracts/operation.v1.md no longer carries one.

title: Split CVG-051 — clause 9's two halves no longer share a disposition after wave 4
description:
Serves documents.v1 Core 9. Found while working converge-12o, which owned the four red rows (CVG-052/053/057/066) and the stale `indexed` refs, and deliberately did not guess at this fifth re-derivation.

CVG-051 is one GAP row quoting the whole of clause 9: "**A work item names its contract** in one line, defines done in plain words, and quotes the feedback or gap it came from." Before wave 4 that was right — rule 4 SKIPped because "work items live in the work queue, not in the repository", and nothing asserted any part of the clause.

Wave 4 replaced that with two rules, and they are no longer the same kind of thing (RAN 2026-09-03, `uv run conformance/documents/run.py . --json-only`):

  9a  work_item_names_a_contract   SKIP  "no work-item export at docs/work-items.json
      and none named with --work-items — work items live in the work queue, not in
      this tree, so the kit has nothing to read"
  9b  work_item_quotes_its_source  SKIP  "measured against this repository's own
      queue: the literal test — a blockquote or a quoted span — passes 7 of 24 real
      items, and most of the 17 it fails do point at their origin … Telling a
      quotation of feedback from a quoted filename needs a reader."

9a is a plain GAP: the check exists, it is mechanical, and it SKIPs only because this repository exports no queue. Supply `docs/work-items.json` (or `--work-items`) and it runs. 9b is a MEASURED refusal — the same shape as rule 7d, which is exactly why converge-jc9 moved CVG-063 to NOT-ASSERTABLE rather than leaving it GAP.

A row whose two halves carry different dispositions is one this ledger splits, quoting a disjoint sentence for each (CVG-059 → CVG-067 in wave 4; CVG-052 → CVG-068 in converge-12o). The likely shape: CVG-051 keeps "**A work item names its contract** in one line, defines done in plain words," as GAP against rule 9a, and a new id takes "and quotes the feedback or gap it came from." as NOT-ASSERTABLE against rule 9b's measurement.

title: Corrected record for converge-nht — its stored resolution contains a retracted false claim that cannot be edited
description:
Serves documents.v1. This item exists to carry a TRUE resolution for work that is finished, because the resolution stored on converge-nht is false and the tracker will not let it be corrected.

WHAT IS WRONG WITH converge-nht's STORED RESOLUTION

It states: "This repository has no ledger — there is no ledger/ directory and no rows.yaml at any commit, and AGENTS.md §3 still says the ledger does not exist yet."

That is false. ledger/rows.yaml is on main (seeded 3c7fdfb; revised c1a4005, bd61d86, d96c379) and on lane/w4-wiring. Lane w4-doc-kit-2 branched at 8b54020, eighteen commits before it landed, so the file is absent from that worktree only. The lane ran `git log -- ledger` against one branch, got nothing, and reported on the repository. `git log --all -- ledger` returns four commits.

It also describes the work as covering "documents.v1 Core 5, 9, 10 and 11". Those are the clauses converge-nht's DESCRIPTION named. The six ledger rows its TITLE and ACCEPTANCE name are Core 1, 2, 6, 7, 12 and 13. The item contradicts itself and the resolution followed the wrong half.

WHY IT CANNOT BE FIXED IN PLACE — both paths tried, both refused

  work_claim(converge-nht)  -> "claim failed: issue not claimable: status closed"
  amplifier-work-tracker resolve --id converge-nht --reason <corrected>
                            -> exit 0, and echoed back the ORIGINAL resolution
                               unchanged (a readback-checked no-op, as the CLI's
                               own help documents)

work_edit / `edit` can rewrite title, description, acceptance and design — every field except the one that is wrong. So the retraction lives on converge-nht's description, in a different field from the claim it retracts, and this item carries the corrected reason in a resolution field where a reader looking at resolutions will actually find it.

Nothing further is to be BUILT here. The work is committed on lane/w4-doc-kit-2 (5fe18cd, acc77b8, ca4036f) and the kit is green. Resolve this item with the corrected reason and read it back; that read-back is the honest evidence converge-nht's own resolution can no longer provide.

The remaining real work — moving the six ledger rows off GAP — is converge-jc9, not this.
acceptance: GIVEN converge-nht's stored resolution, which cannot be edited, WHEN this item is resolved and read back THEN its stored reason states what the lane actually did, names the six ledger rows by the clauses they really cover, and retracts the false claim about the ledger in the field a reader checks; AND the link from this item to converge-nht makes the replacement findable from either end.
